title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 10 of the notes on the structure at infinity of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν} (page numbered 44 by Grothendieck). Section title: 'Discrete MDT structure: notion of MD-morphisms of normalization between graphs'.

Context. In the preceding sections the strata M_G of the Mumford–Deligne compactification, indexed by 'MD-graphs' G (dual graphs of stable curves), carry 'tubular' fundamental groupoids. ΠM_G is the fundamental groupoid of the stratum. SΠM_G is an extension of ΠM_G by Z^{A(G)}, one Z for each double point, given by the loop around that node. Two kinds of maps have been made functorial so far:
- SΠf, for f a 'generalization' morphism G→G/C, i.e. a contraction of a set C of edges;
- Πf, for f an isomorphism of MD-graphs.
The previous page imposes a compatibility diagram (125) for these.

The problem. In the course of the work, two further maps occurred that are not of this kind:
(i) M_G → M_{g_α, Î_α}, from the stratum to the moduli of the normalized component at a vertex α, whose marked points Î_α include the branches over the nodes;
(ii) M^π_{g,I} → M_{g,I'} for I'⊂I. This is a 'bord de la tranche' (boundary of a tubular neighbourhood) type map that drops the points of I∖I'.

The proposal. Grothendieck introduces a second class of morphisms of MD-graphs, the 'normalization morphisms'. Their intersection with the class of generalization morphisms is exactly the isomorphisms.

Geometric meaning. Take a stable curve X = X̂∖I over an algebraically closed field k, with I the points at infinity and A the double points. Choose subsets I'⊂I and A'⊂A. The next page then builds X' = X̂'∖I', where X̂' is the partial normalization of X̂ at A∖A', and the points of I∖I' are treated through the 'bord de la tranche'. Combinatorially this is the data of:
- a spanning subgraph C'⊂C (same vertex set, edge set A');
- a subset I'⊂I of the legs.
The dual graph of X' is that subgraph.

In modern terms: the 'discrete' (combinatorial) skeleton of the Teichmüller tower gets two generating classes of morphisms. Edge contractions are specializations/generalizations. Edge-deletion plus leg-deletion are cutting/normalization and forgetting points. These are the combinatorial counterparts of clutching/gluing maps and forgetful maps.
errors: Forgetting the points of I∖I' while keeping only the nodes in A' can destroy stability. A component may become genus 0 with fewer than 3 special points, or genus 1 with none. A stabilization (contraction) step, or a restriction on (I',A'), seems needed. It is not addressed on this page; perhaps the 'bord de la tranche' interpretation sidesteps it, but that is not visible here.
On the next page, the warning that X̂' maps only to X̂ and not to the full normalization unless I'=I is somewhat unclear as written. It is a minor point.

ideas.what: Category of MD-graphs (stable dual graphs) with two classes of morphisms: generalization (edge contraction) and normalization (spanning-subgraph / leg-subset). The two classes intersect exactly in the isomorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs with contractions and cuttings/forgetful morphisms (modular operad structure; graph categories of Getzler–Kapranov, Behrend–Manin; tropical moduli categories of Chan–Galatius–Payne)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the 'Lego–Teichmüller' tower built from operations of cutting and erasing points. The explicit graph-morphism formalism is not published there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Maps from a boundary stratum to the moduli of its normalized components, and forgetful maps M_{g,I}→M_{g,I'}, viewed as induced by graph morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Clutching/gluing maps and forgetful (point-erasing) morphisms of M̄_{g,n}

ideas.what: Normalization data described as (spanning subgraph C'⊂C with the same vertices, subset I'⊂I of legs)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's unpublished, explicit attempt to make the tubular fundamental groupoids SΠM_G functorial for a two-sided category of dual graphs (contractions and normalizations/forgetting) anticipates later work. Examples are Bakalov–Kirillov's Lego–Teichmüller game and the 'stable graph' categories of modular operads. Specialists in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory may know this only through the Esquisse sketch.
missed.quote: On va introduire pour ceci une notion de morphisme de MD-graphes, contenant notion de morphismes de normalisation (l'intersection des deux notions de morphisme est celle d'iso de MD-graphes).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a documented precursor of the operadic/graph-categorical formulation of the profinite Teichmüller tower. It is historically interesting but does not appear to contain a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a natural combinatorial notion of morphisms between dual graphs of stable curves (contraction versus deletion of edges/legs). This is now standard (modular operads, stable graph categories). It is of historical interest as an early, detailed version of the Lego–Teichmüller framework, but contains no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: Top line: page number '44' and section number '10)'. 'MDT' is as written.
Third display: the source is written M^π_{g,I}. The superscript is hard to read and could also be another symbol.
